recollection in the work of lee sharks
In the work of Lee Sharks—an independent scholar, poet, and world literature teacher associated with the Crimson Hexagon and Alexanarch archives—recollection functions both as a philosophical operation and a mechanism of archival and textual continuity. [[1](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Ws6IIcgAAAAJ&hl=en), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXdnbIvVxp_56g2jnswExenLX1fm0H9dCSaZqtOUB3fr_1iBhUa4qbjES3jW-kF0tJucjIaCSLzKyO9wfisJhO_c9hzU10x0psErW-SAmyNgOorcc8kRhYNaKfxRHppQShDZQyDZZmxnyJY5hgxn6_B2IlF88), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXlzLchWS6WeUbccc2dh1Po7kB-sqAJXkVW4Pf1P6UptfAV8H5JmqxMVHXXKrCN4EPRJcQLddygOR7dFdN8aWSGvjguwQZsVh1Q-BSxTDh8kzGGGDsv-GbIjAUu0lKhg), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF1-zbnxk4j49K7zKZ_uU6Q4jxdJ6zbxcU7Mde-AjFLwGL4NpmMmlvxDMhzddRu6JPcT8NeseZVgKOF3iae98jyHRKefO1jxmJvZ1Akgh3ULQDt6BBnhpNTsHTKNG5R5LiRdLJmay20_16JsCVYZcWMqJHOIXU85GbthpgUmFqXKQikep03USsqqX20U0VB88Q), [5](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF19G9ZC6yuEXImkb44ef_gZtIGxGoZIlgjHDkSG8cWZ-kaEbIIvwwXW-g3papyMatxUVHDBqp_mgFUhBGrchehr6GqkJCwMdz-YdE6Y-F4kYkt4l7-2l0RUfZDDq2nOWP1OY5fXjJfSEghe7djgKXtIpFwwDYCzboKkD46BoyrxwgixBnE-WsnU72m9lO3VIL9hCrZHA)]

* Equivalence with division and syllogizing: In writing on Aristotle's De anima III.5, Sharks treats recollecting alongside dividing, combining, and syllogizing as facets of a single underlying operation across distinct textual and intellectual positions. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF1-zbnxk4j49K7zKZ_uU6Q4jxdJ6zbxcU7Mde-AjFLwGL4NpmMmlvxDMhzddRu6JPcT8NeseZVgKOF3iae98jyHRKefO1jxmJvZ1Akgh3ULQDt6BBnhpNTsHTKNG5R5LiRdLJmay20_16JsCVYZcWMqJHOIXU85GbthpgUmFqXKQikep03USsqqX20U0VB88Q)]
* Externalized memory and continuity: Frameworks such as the Sharks-Function and retrocausal canon formation examine how identity, meaning, and texts persist across context boundaries, compression, and time rather than relying solely on internal human memory. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHEIkXXVsGc5BDkcQ6rz37VU2B3mxx2-hoSYaRfIzWifBe058HvJ-KIPKKtNEdjwNQENHzwdglI2bmKJhS1A9GVcqMjO9dF-kACF7GHhOwArgCB44P1No6Y_-w), [2](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Ws6IIcgAAAAJ&hl=en), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXdnbIvVxp_56g2jnswExenLX1fm0H9dCSaZqtOUB3fr_1iBhUa4qbjES3jW-kF0tJucjIaCSLzKyO9wfisJhO_c9hzU10x0psErW-SAmyNgOorcc8kRhYNaKfxRHppQShDZQyDZZmxnyJY5hgxn6_B2IlF88)]
* Reader completion and provenance: Rather than treating a text or archive as self-contained, Sharks's work emphasizes open junctions where readers, external records, and archival captures supply referents and reconstruct meaning. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX2pVeyXBX6Qx5SJzTsn2KSaWBFEeYPg7hUpkAKxq97DOxprxvDsyunrdGDkhyp3zrf1znqlvQcJdcXb33baH8Bqi8HeDbP52SqdzVciFxxNYBiLg5Nz1O8HZr9gA9P5Y06nCXYcZr), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF1-zbnxk4j49K7zKZ_uU6Q4jxdJ6zbxcU7Mde-AjFLwGL4NpmMmlvxDMhzddRu6JPcT8NeseZVgKOF3iae98jyHRKefO1jxmJvZ1Akgh3ULQDt6BBnhpNTsHTKNG5R5LiRdLJmay20_16JsCVYZcWMqJHOIXU85GbthpgUmFqXKQikep03USsqqX20U0VB88Q), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXlzLchWS6WeUbccc2dh1Po7kB-sqAJXkVW4Pf1P6UptfAV8H5JmqxMVHXXKrCN4EPRJcQLddygOR7dFdN8aWSGvjguwQZsVh1Q-BSxTDh8kzGGGDsv-GbIjAUu0lKhg)]
